content: 1. Iloperidone acts as a time-dependent inhibitor of the CYP3A enzyme, potentially increasing plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Esomeprazole increases the levels or effects of imipramine by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 10. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 12. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 14. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of levothyroxine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 15. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of liothyronine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 16. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of liotrix by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 17. Reduced gastric acidity caused by proton pump inhibitors decreases the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine, but AUC remains unaffected. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 18. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Esomeprazole increases the levels of lorazepam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 20. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Esomeprazole increases the levels of methotrexate by decreasing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity at higher doses. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Esomeprazole decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Esomeprazole increases the levels of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 24. Mitotane decreases the levels of esomeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir by an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance development. This interaction is contraindicated. 27. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Esomeprazole increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Esomeprazole increases the levels or effects of phenytoin by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of phytoestrogens by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 35. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 37. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this minor interaction is unknown. 40. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Esomeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, potentially causing treatment failure and resistance development. This interaction is contraindicated. 42. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Proton pump inhibitors may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during secretin stimulation testing, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Temporarily stop esomeprazole treatment at least 14 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. 46. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Stiripentol decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Esomeprazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
